subject: Embeddings migration & integration - vector dims, batching, auth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps — embeddings migration

Hi Alex / Jordan,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the Acme search team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone's aligned: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Current setup: Acme is on OtherEmbed provider, embeddings are 768-dim; search uses cosine similarity on normalized vectors stored in Postgres (pgvector).
- Pain points: cost at scale, inconsistent vector norms after vendor switch, and slow bulk re-indexing windows.
- Goals: match or improve quality (precision@k), reduce per-query cost, and have a predictable migration path with minimal downtime.

Action items / recommended approach (high level):
1) Migration strategy: bulk re-embed all documents in controlled batches and write to a new index namespace to enable A/B before cutover.
   - Suggested batch size: start with 1k-5k docs per job, tune up to 10k depending on throughput and memory.
2) Vector dim / model: we recommend moving to a 1536-dim embedding (Redwood-embed-1536) for higher semantic capacity; we can benchmark against a 768 baseline.
3) Normalization: normalize on-write (L2) to keep query-time costs down; keep raw vectors in a cold store if you want to experiment with alternative scoring.
4) Batching & throughput: use continuous batching in the Redwood SDK + our bulk migration helper (we'll share sample code).
5) Auth / routing: use API keys scoped to the migration job or short-lived mTLS tokens for dedicated infra; route heavy migration traffic to dedicated capacity to avoid impacting production queries.

Attachments: redwood-embeddings-migration-checklist.pdf (migration checklist + sample scripts) and a sample CSV mapping file.

Proposed next steps:
- Dev: we'll share the bulk migration snippet and an initial cost/time estimate by EOD today. (Action: @dev_patel)
- Acme: confirm whether you prefer to re-embed everything or maintain hybrid approach per index. Also share an estimate of total docs and average document size.
- Schedule a 30m follow-up next week to review the benchmark results and finalize cutover plan.

Timing: if you want to move fast, we can run a 10k-doc pilot this week and share results within 48 hours.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

4) Auth: currently we're using API keys for OtherEmbed. For Redwood, is API key sufficient for large-scale migration jobs or do you recommend mTLS / IAM-based short-lived tokens?

5) Sample code: can you send the bulk migration helper and an example parallelism strategy (how many workers, retries, backoff)?

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps — embeddings migration (technical notes)

Hi Alex — quick technical notes to address the questions: 

Vector dimensions / model selection:
- 1536-dim embeddings (e.g., redwood-embed-1536) generally give better capacity for semantic tasks vs 768, particularly for longer docs. That said, improvements are workload-dependent. We'll run a small benchmark: sample 2k queries against both dims and report precision@10 and MRR.

Normalization strategy:
- Two common patterns: normalize-on-write (store normalized vectors) or normalize-on-query.
  - Normalize-on-write: cheaper per-query (cosine becomes dot product if vectors are normalized) and avoids per-query compute; preferred if you control ingestion.
  - Normalize-on-query: keeps raw vectors but adds CPU at query time; OK if you need to keep raw magnitude info.
- Recommendation: normalize-on-write for your main index, keep a raw vector backup in cold storage for experiments.

Batching / throughput / migration sizing:
- For embeddings, batching by documents per request is most efficient. We typically see best throughput with batch sizes between 256–2048 vectors depending on GPU memory and model (start at 512).
- For 2.3M docs, re-embedding in 10k increments (10k docs per job) with parallel workers (10–20 workers) is a pragmatic starting point. That lets you complete a full re-index in ~1–2 days depending on model and infra.

Auth / routing:
- API keys are fine for most customers. For large bulk jobs we recommend scoped API keys plus routing to a dedicated pool ("migration" tag) to avoid impacting production endpoints. If you require stronger guarantees use short-lived mTLS or IAM-based tokens.

Sample Redwood SDK snippet (bulk embed + write):
```
# pseudocode
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", route="migration-pool")
for batch in batches(docs, size=512):
    embs = client.embeddings.create(model="redwood-embed-1536", inputs=batch)
    # perform L2 normalization server-side or save normalized vectors
    client.store.upsert(namespace="acme_v2", vectors=normalize(embs))
```

Retries and backoff:
- Use exponential backoff with jitter; mark idempotency via doc IDs so retries are safe.

I'll prepare a short benchmark script and cost estimate for the 10k pilot and send by EOD.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Thanks Dev — that helps. A couple follow-ups: 

- We lean toward re-embedding everything but still want to measure quality delta. Please include sample precision@K on the pilot.
- Can you give a rough cost estimate (compute + tokens) for re-embedding 10k docs with 1536-dim model and the benchmark run?
- For batching: we use k8s workers; 10–20 workers sounds fine. What memory footprint do you expect per worker for 512 vs 1024 vectors?

Also, we'll need a shutdown-safe migration plan (if a worker fails mid-job, no partial index corruption). We'll work with your upsert semantics but want to confirm idempotency guarantees.

Let's schedule the pilot kickoff call — I'm available tomorrow morning. Please send an invite.

—Alex

Alex — great, thanks for the quick replies. Attached is a short migration plan and the sample mapping CSV you requested (sample-mapping.csv). Key points and next steps: 

1) Pilot scope: 10k docs, run both 768 (baseline) and 1536 (redwood-embed-1536) to compare precision@10 and latency. We'll provide perf + quality matrices within 48 hours of pilot completion.

2) Cost estimate (rough):
- Pilot embed compute: ~ $120–$250 depending on chosen instance and concurrency (we'll provide exact once you confirm worker size).
- Full re-embed (2.3M docs): rough order of magnitude ~ $25k–$60k compute-only; we will give a formal quote if you want Redwood-managed migration.

3) Idempotency & safety: our upsert is idempotent by vector ID; failed jobs can be retried safely. We recommend writing to a new namespace (acme_v2) and switching aliases once the benchmark is validated.

4) Auth & routing: we'll issue a scoped API key for the migration and tag traffic to the dedicated "migration" pool. If you prefer mTLS for the migration key rotation, we can enable that as well.

5) Logistics: please provide:
- Estimated total docs and an S3 export (or access to a sample 50k docs)
- A contact for infra to coordinate workers and rate limits
